paragraphs: Dear Theophilus — in my first book I wrote down everything Jesus started doing and teaching, right up to the day he said goodbye to the apostles he had chosen through the Holy Spirit and was taken up to heaven. After he died, he showed up alive to them again and again, in all kinds of situations, over forty days. Face to face, he talked with them about the kingdom of God.

Over meals together, he gave them a firm order: don't leave Jerusalem under any circumstances — wait for what the Father promised, the promise you heard from me. John baptized people in water, but you are about to be baptized in the Holy Spirit. And it's happening soon.
When they were together for the last time, they asked him, "Master, is this the time? Are you going to restore the kingdom to Israel right now?"

He told them, "The timing isn't yours to know — that's the Father's business. What you will get is the Holy Spirit. When the Holy Spirit comes on you, you'll have what it takes to be my witnesses — in Jerusalem, all over Judea and Samaria, and all the way to the ends of the world."

Those were his last words. While they watched, he was lifted up and disappeared into a cloud. They just stood there, staring into the empty sky. Then suddenly two men in white robes appeared beside them. "You Galileans!" they said. "Why are you just standing here staring up at an empty sky? This same Jesus, taken up from you into heaven, will come back just as surely — and just as mysteriously — as he left."

So they headed back to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives — just a little over half a mile away. They went up to the upper room where they had been meeting: Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas the son of James.
They were all in this together for good — united in prayer, the women included, plus Mary the mother of Jesus and his brothers.

During those days, Peter stood up in front of the group — about 120 people were gathered — and said, "Friends, the Scripture had to come true: the one where the Holy Spirit spoke through David about Judas, the man who guided the soldiers to arrest Jesus. And now it has. Judas was one of us; he had his own assigned place in this ministry."

"You all know what happened: he took that evil bribe money and bought a little farm. That's where he came to a terrible end — his belly burst open and his guts spilled out. Everybody in Jerusalem knows the story; they call that place Murder Meadow. It's exactly what the Psalms said: 'Let his farm become a haunted ruin, so no one can ever live there.' And later: 'Let someone else take over his position.'"

"So Judas has to be replaced. The replacement must come from the men who stuck with us the whole time — from when John baptized Jesus all the way to the day Jesus was taken up to heaven — someone who, like us, is designated as a witness to his resurrection."

They nominated two men: Joseph Barsabbas, nicknamed Justus, and Matthias. Then they prayed: "Lord, you know every one of us inside and out. Show us clearly which of these two you've chosen to take the place in this ministry and leadership that Judas threw away to go his own way." Then they drew straws — and Matthias won. He was counted in with the eleven apostles.
